meta.titre: Invoices and Credit Notes: working out bills and correcting errors
meta.sous_theme: Contents of an invoice, discount and VAT, credit notes and debit notes

sections.contenu_markdown: A baker in Bamenda orders flour on credit. The supplier delivers the bags together with a document that lists what was sold, at what price and how much must be paid. When two bags arrive torn, the baker does not simply pay less on a whim: the supplier sends a second document that cancels part of the bill. These documents are the invoice, the credit note and the debit note. The GCE Commerce papers ask what each one is, when it is used and how its amounts are worked out.

items: Quantity multiplied by unit price gives the amount for each item.
A percentage of an amount is found by multiplying the amount by the rate and dividing by 100.
Goods bought on credit are paid for after delivery.
A trade discount is a reduction in the list price given to a trader who buys goods for resale.

sections.titre: The invoice, the credit note and the debit note
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The invoice

An **invoice** is a document sent by the seller to the buyer for goods sold on credit. It records the details of one transaction and tells the buyer how much to pay. It shows the names and addresses of both parties, the invoice number and date, a description of the goods, the quantity and unit price, any trade discount, any VAT, the amount due and the terms of payment. The seller records it as a sale; the buyer checks it against the order and the delivery note and records it as a purchase.

### How the amount due is worked out

1. Gross total = quantity × unit price, added over all items.
2. Subtract the **trade discount** to get the net amount.
3. Add **VAT** (value added tax) on the net amount, at the rate given in the question.
4. The result is the amount due.

A **cash discount** is different: it is offered for quick payment and is deducted only if the buyer pays in time, so it is not taken off on the invoice itself.

### The credit note

A **credit note** is sent by the seller to reduce the amount the buyer owes. It is issued when goods are returned, when goods are damaged or faulty and an allowance is given, or when the invoice **overcharged** the buyer. It is often printed in red to tell it apart from an invoice.

### The debit note

A **debit note** is sent by the seller when the invoice **undercharged** the buyer, so that an extra amount is added to what is owed.

### Quick guide

| Situation | Document |
|---|---|
| Goods returned or damaged | Credit note |
| Invoice charged too much | Credit note |
| Invoice charged too little | Debit note |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must work out the value of a credit note for returned goods
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use the **same unit price, the same trade discount rate and the same VAT rate** as on the invoice. Work out the gross value of the returned goods, subtract the trade discount, then add VAT. The new balance owed is the amount due on the invoice minus the credit note.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question mentions a document sent before the goods are supplied
variantes.contenu_markdown: A **pro forma invoice** is sent before the sale is completed. It shows what the invoice would contain, so that the buyer can decide, arrange payment or obtain approval. It is not a demand for payment and is not recorded as a sale.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When two documents seem to do the same job
variantes.contenu_markdown: An invoice asks for payment of goods supplied on credit. A **receipt** is given after payment to confirm that money has been received.

sections.enonce_markdown: A wholesaler sells 20 bags of rice at 25,000 FCFA each and 10 cartons of tinned tomatoes at 12,000 FCFA each to a retailer on credit. A trade discount of 10% is allowed and VAT at 10% is charged on the net amount. The rates are hypothetical. Later, 4 cartons of tomatoes are returned as damaged. (a) Prepare the invoice. (b) Prepare the credit note for the returned cartons. (c) State the amount the retailer now owes.

etapes.justification: Quantity × unit price for each item, then add.

etapes.action: Deduct the trade discount and add VAT
etapes.justification: The discount is taken off first, and VAT is charged on what remains.
Show every line so that the buyer can check the amounts.
etapes.resultat_markdown:
| Item | Quantity | Unit price (FCFA) | Amount (FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bags of rice (50 kg) | 20 | 25,000 | 500,000 |
| Cartons of tinned tomatoes | 10 | 12,000 | 120,000 |
| Gross total | | | 620,000 |
| Less trade discount 10% | | | 62,000 |
| Net amount | | | 558,000 |
| Add VAT 10% | | | 55,800 |
| **Amount due** | | | **613,800** |

etapes.justification: Same price, same discount rate and same VAT rate as the invoice.
etapes.resultat_markdown:
| Item | Quantity | Unit price (FCFA) | Amount (FCFA) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cartons of tinned tomatoes returned | 4 | 12,000 | 48,000 |
| Less trade discount 10% | | | 4,800 |
| Net amount | | | 43,200 |
| Add VAT 10% | | | 4,320 |
| **Credit note total** | | | **47,520** |

etapes.justification: The credit note reduces the amount owed.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **The invoice is for 613,800 FCFA, the credit note is for 47,520 FCFA and the retailer now owes 566,280 FCFA.** Check: 20 bags of rice and 6 cartons of tomatoes come to 572,000 FCFA gross; after the 10% discount and 10% VAT this gives 566,280 FCFA, the same result.

items.erreur_markdown: Charging VAT on the gross total before the trade discount is taken off
items.pourquoi_faux: VAT is charged on the amount the buyer actually pays for the goods, which is the net amount after the trade discount.
items.correction_markdown: Gross total, less trade discount, equals the net amount; then add VAT on the net amount.

items.erreur_markdown: Deducting a cash discount on the invoice for every buyer
items.pourquoi_faux: A cash discount is given only if the buyer pays within the agreed time. It is not part of the invoice calculation.
items.correction_markdown: Deduct the trade discount on the invoice; allow the cash discount later, when prompt payment is made.

items.erreur_markdown: Using a debit note to correct an overcharge or to deal with returned goods
items.pourquoi_faux: A debit note increases the amount owed. An overcharge and returns reduce it.
items.correction_markdown: Use a credit note for overcharges and returns; use a debit note for an undercharge.

items.erreur_markdown: Making a credit note at a different price or without the discount and VAT of the invoice
items.pourquoi_faux: The credit note must cancel exactly the part of the invoice that is wrong, with the same rates.
items.correction_markdown: Use the invoice unit price, then apply the same trade discount rate and the same VAT rate.

items.erreur_markdown: 'An invoice is the document given to the buyer after payment.'
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes a receipt. An invoice asks for payment.
items.correction_markdown: The invoice is sent with or after the goods and requests payment; the receipt confirms that payment has been made.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the document that the seller should send in each case: (a) a customer returns faulty goods; (b) an invoice charged for 15 items but 20 were delivered; (c) a buyer wants to see the expected price of a machine before ordering it; (d) an invoice was added up wrongly and the customer was charged too much.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Credit note**: the amount owed falls. (b) **Debit note**: the buyer was undercharged and owes more. (c) **Pro forma invoice**: it shows the price in advance and is not a demand for payment. (d) **Credit note**: an overcharge is corrected by reducing the amount owed.

items.enonce_markdown: A school supplier sells 40 uniforms at 3,500 FCFA each. A trade discount of 20% is given and VAT of 10% (a hypothetical rate) is added on the net amount. Calculate the amount due on the invoice.

A builder agreed to buy 30 bags of cement at 4,800 FCFA a bag, with a trade discount of 5% and VAT of 10% on the net amount (hypothetical rates). The supplier's invoice charged 5,200 FCFA a bag by mistake. (a) State the document that corrects the mistake. (b) Calculate the amount of the invoice as issued and the amount that should have been charged. (c) Calculate the value of the correcting document and show that it agrees with your answer to (b).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The invoice overcharged the buyer, so the supplier sends a **credit note**.

(b) As issued: $30 \times 5\,200 = 156\,000$; less 5% gives $148\,200$; plus 10% VAT gives **163,020 FCFA**.

Correct: $30 \times 4\,800 = 144\,000$; less 5% gives $136\,800$; plus 10% VAT gives **150,480 FCFA**.

(c) Price error per bag $= 5\,200 - 4\,800 = 400$, so for 30 bags $= 12\,000$ FCFA. Less 5% discount gives $11\,400$; plus 10% VAT gives **12,540 FCFA**.

Check: $163\,020 - 150\,480 = 12\,540$, so the credit note brings the amount due down to the correct figure.

items_markdown: An invoice is sent by the seller for goods sold on credit and shows the quantity, unit price, discounts, VAT and the amount due.
Amount due = gross total - trade discount + VAT, with VAT charged on the net amount after the trade discount.
A cash discount is for prompt payment and is not deducted on the invoice.
A credit note reduces what the buyer owes (returns, damaged goods, overcharge); a debit note increases it (undercharge).
A credit note uses the same price, discount rate and VAT rate as the invoice it corrects.
A pro forma invoice is a preview sent before the sale; a receipt is issued after payment.
